final:
None of the 7 review comments needs a code change. Five are invalid, one is only partly right, and one is a style preference. I didn't change any code or post replies. The verdicts are in `verdicts.json`, and the file parses as valid JSON.

Issues 1–5 all ask for fixes "to satisfy Ruff," but this repo doesn't run Ruff. Its linter is flake8 (`.pre-commit-config.yaml:43-47`, `setup.cfg:87-95`).

| # | Category | Verdict | Actionable | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Correctness | Partly valid | Optional | Nothing checks `num_queues` (`queue_consumer.py:202`), but the only caller passes `max_workers or 20`, so a 0 becomes 20 and the division error can't happen from the command line. A negative value fails differently: `IndexError` at `queue_consumer.py:209`. A `num_queues >= 1` check would be cheap to add. |
| 1 | Best practice | Invalid | No | `join(timeout)` has to match the signature that arroyo's `ProcessingStrategy` requires, and no linter here flags the unused parameter. |
| 2 | Nitpick | Invalid | No | The test callback has to accept the same `(identifier, result)` arguments that the queue workers pass it (`queue_consumer.py:140`). |
| 3 | Nitpick | Invalid | No | `track_calls` is a mock side effect and has to take the processor's `(identifier, result)` arguments. |
| 4 | Nitpick | Invalid | No | `force` mirrors arroyo's `Commit` interface (the same file calls `commit(offsets, force)` at line 2077). Renaming it to `_force` would break any caller that passes `force=` by name. |
| 5 | Convention | Invalid | No | The rule cited is Ruff-only. `pytestmark = [requires_kafka]` appears 9 times in the tests and the tuple form never does, and the list is never modified. |
| 6 | Best practice | Style preference | No | The `except Exception: pass` is best-effort topic cleanup in a test's `finally` block, so a cleanup failure can't hide the real test result. The same pattern appears 9 times in the tests. |

One thing the reviewer didn't raise, related to issue 1: `join()` ignores its `timeout` argument and always uses the fixed 5-second waits inside `close()`. That might be worth a look, but it isn't what the reviewer flagged, so it doesn't change that verdict.
